thread:
alex_cs: FYI customer reported a sudden spike of 503s starting ~09:12 UTC. They say their batch-size update rolled out and then errors started.
emma_support: Which customer / model? any repro payload?
alex_cs: AcmeMaps, model=redwood-3b-v1 hosted, traffic ~120 qps. They pushed an SDK change that increased client-side batch to 64 -> previously 16. Failures across multiple regions.
ryan_sre: Seeing alerts: upstream inference workers in pool 'hosted-gpu-prod-8' restarting. 503 surge correlated with worker restarts.
jamie_runtime: Can you paste the runner logs?
alex_cs: Pasting key snippet from hosted logs (sanitized):
```
E 09:12:44.123 runner[pid=2145]: allocating KV cache for seq_len=2048 batch=64 -> requested 31.8GiB
W 09:12:44.124 runner[pid=2145]: gpu mem before alloc: 10.2GiB free
E 09:12:44.126 runner[pid=2145]: cudaErrorMemoryAllocation: out of memory
I 09:12:44.127 runner[pid=2145]: attempting graceful shutdown
Segmentation fault (core dumped)
```
ryan_sre: That's a classic OOM during a batch resize event. But segfault after OOM usually indicates attempt to access freed pointer (race in KV prefetch).
sena_ml: Did the change only affect client-side batching or did they also switch to longer seq lengths?
alex_cs: They increased batch only. seq_len stays at 1024.
jamie_runtime: The log shows seq_len=2048 in allocation. suspect autoscaler or model config change triggered a different context (maybe per-request prompt expanded by system messages). Could be prefix caching blowup.
ryan_sre: I pulled node metrics around 09:12. GPU memory spikes to full then watchdog kills runner -> container restart. Restart loop lasted ~7m, causing 503 fanout.
infra-bot: deploy-bot reported a simultaneous autoscaler upscale for pool hosted-gpu-prod-8 at 09:11:59 (policy: batch-adaptive).
jamie_runtime: If autoscaler increases batch capacity while existing workers still handling inflight requests, there might be a transient allocation mismatch. Need repro.
emma_support: Customer is blocked, requests ETA. Any mitigation we can do quick?
ryan_sre: Immediate mitigations: 1) Route traffic to backup pool 'hosted-gpu-std-3' (lower bsize but stable) 2) Temporarily disable batch-adaptive autoscaling for that pool 3) Rollback client-side batch change if possible.
sena_ml: Also recommend enabling compressed KV/quantized model variant for that customer (uses ~40% less memory).
jamie_runtime: Technical triage steps: collect coredump from one restarted container, capture nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY during repro, get runner binary + symbol build id.
ryan_sre: Repro steps I ran in staging: triggered batch resize via test harness:
```
# harness simplified
python send_load.py --qps 200 --batch 64 --seq 1024 --model redwood-3b-v1
# monitor
watch -n1 nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used --format=csv
```
Result: worker attempted to allocate >30GB, failed, segfault after OOM in kv_prefetch.c:read_prefetch+0x1f2.
jamie_runtime: That symbol matches a known race from earlier runtime change (prefetch fork optimization) — we pushed partial fix but didn't backport to hosted GA build.
emma_support: Can we patch-host? how long?
jamie_runtime: Fast path: revert the prefetch optimization in the build deployed to hosted pool and roll. Estimated ~2-3 hours to build/test/roll with canary.
ryan_sre: Meanwhile I'm pausing autoscaler and routing traffic to std pool. Also bumping node ephemeral memory limit.
infra-bot: Action logged: paused autoscaler policy 'batch-adaptive' for hosted-gpu-prod-8 by ryan_sre @ 09:28 UTC.
alex_cs: Customer accepted temporary routing. They asked for repro steps so they can rollback client change.
sena_ml: For long-term prevention: add runtime guard to cap per-request allocation to (gpu_mem - safety_margin) and fail gracefully with 429 instructing client to reduce batch.
jamie_runtime: Agree. Also we should add preflight estimator in SDK that fails locally when requested batch would exceed recommended tokens-per-GPU.
emma_support: Any immediate logs I should collect for customer? request id, container id?
ryan_sre: Yes: get request_id from 503 responses, container id and node id from request headers X-Runner-ID / X-Node-ID, and we already captured core and exporter snapshots. Send to S3 bucket s3://redwood-incident-dumps/2987654321/ .
jamie_runtime: I'll prepare a debug build with prefetch revert and a test patch. If QA green, plan canary to 10% in 30m, then ramp.
emma_support: Communicated to customer: temporary routing in place, we expect reduced 503s. ETA for fix ~3-4 hours, will update in 30m. :thumbsup:
alex_cs: Customer replied thanks, will pause client batch rollout.
ryan_sre: Followups: collect GPU coredump (gdb -c core /opt/runner/bin/runner), include /proc/<pid>/maps from crash, and dmesg for cuda errors. Also add alert rule to fire when restart rate > 5/min.
jamie_runtime: Noted. I'll open a PR with revert and runtime guard RFC.
infra-bot: Created ticket INFRA-4921 "runner: cap allocation during dynamic batch resize" assigned to jamie_runtime.
emma_support: Closing loop for now. Will post postmortem if customer impact persists.
ryan_sre: I'll leave temporary autoscaler pause until patch rolled.
jamie_runtime: Thanks everyone. Logging key artifacts to the incident folder and will post patch link once PR is open.
alex_cs: Marking this thread resolved for handoff
